decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate 0.0 confirms whole-row uniqueness, but flight_number's distinct_count 2994 against row_count 166158 shows numbers repeat across dates, so date, carrier, flight number, and origin together form the smallest plausible identifying tuple, unverified until measured.

dep_hhmm, dep_delay_minutes, arr_hhmm, arr_delay_minutes, air_time_minutes (null_rate ~0.03) and aircraft_manufacturer, aircraft_model, aircraft_manufacture_year, aircraft_seat_count, aircraft_engine_type (null_rate ~0.16-0.18) and tail_number (0.009) and dest_* fields (0.02089) are retained as nullable per their profiled null rates rather than dropped.
dep_delay_minutes min -33 and arr_delay_minutes min -86 show early arrivals and departures are legitimate, so no non_negative rule is proposed for these two columns.

captured_at values cluster within seconds on 2026-09-02, indicating a pipeline capture clock rather than flight data; retained as a column per rule 1 though it is not flagged is_airbyte_metadata in this profile.

is_cancelled's distinct_values false and true are native booleans not strings, and logical_type boolean already enforces the domain, so no accepted_values_subset rule is proposed for it to avoid a type mismatch.

purpose: This table holds individual commercial flight records departing NYC-area airports (EWR, JFK, LGA) across the first half of 2013, combining schedule, actual timing, delay, carrier, aircraft, and airport reference attributes into one denormalized row per flight.
usage: Read the table at the grain of one row per flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number, and origin_airport; join to the actual dep/arr HHMM and delay columns to compute on-time performance, and expect dep_hhmm, arr_hhmm, dep_delay_minutes, arr_delay_minutes, and air_time_minutes to be null for flights that never departed or arrived (is_cancelled true or otherwise unresolved).
limitations: The profile cannot confirm the proposed grain is truly unique until a deterministic measurement checks it against the warehouse; roughly 16-18% of rows lack aircraft registration detail (manufacturer, model, year, seats, engine type) and about 2% lack destination airport reference detail, so joins on those fields will silently miss rows; tail_number, dep/arr timing, and delay columns are null for a small share of rows and that nullability is a profiled fact, not a data quality defect to be fixed here; captured_at appears to be a pipeline ingestion timestamp despite not being flagged as airbyte metadata in this profile, and a reviewer should confirm its intended semantics.
